platforms.language: Rwanda: 13 of 51 captions in Kinyarwanda, most English, French on 1. Property and cheap-goods ads lean Kinyarwanda; hotels, clinics, tech and beauty lean English. Tanzania: Swahili. Kenya and Uganda: English. Numbers as people write them (38,000 RWF, 48K, 400K, 350M RWF).
findings: Caption corpus (125 captions, 111 Rwandan): phone or WhatsApp in 63%, a place in 77%, a price or offer in 58%, a call to action in 71%, a delivery promise in 30%; all four of phone, price, place and call to action in 29 rows.
Hashtags: Facebook ads median 1 (49% none; 5 when used), Facebook reels 0, TikTok 5.
Numbers: mostly 10-digit local with no spaces (0788218567); 22 with +250 and spaces; two numbers are common; the label is 'Call/WhatsApp:'.
Prices: '20,000 RWF', '48,000RWF', '38000FRW', '18k gusa', 'Price:3.5M', '35K → 27K'; the currency comes as RWF, FRW, Rwf, rfw, frw.

Language (Rwandan rows): English 77, mixed 19, Kinyarwanda 14, French 1. Kinyarwanda for plots, houses, cheap goods and baby products; mixed for food, phones and fashion; English for hotels, clinics, tech and beauty.
Kinyarwanda calls to action: Duhamagare, Twandikire, uhamagare kuri, twandikire cg uduhamagare; 'kuri {price} gusa' before a price.
Addresses are landmarks, not streets: 'Next to DELIGHT HOTEL', 'opposite IPRC traffic lights', 'Makuza Peace Plaza, Room 35', 'same building as boho, door 8'.
13 of 51 captions are in Kinyarwanda; most are English; 1 is French. Cleopatra Home writes the caption twice, English then Kinyarwanda.
Median video length 34 s; about half under 30 s (under 20 s for products and offers, 40 to 90 s with a talking person).
The caption carries the spec list (checklist emojis: price, size, area, water and power, title, delivery); the video is the proof, the caption is the contract.
MoMo is rare: none of the first 51 ads or the 111 Rwandan captions mentions it; the Sofar Kigali ticket ad does ('MoMo: 0788617015').

Long runners (20 Rwandan ads live 97 to 565 days): 11 of 20 put a number in the caption; hashtags 0 to 12, median 2 to 3, 8 of 20 none; openers are plain statements or one question ('Need a furniture upgrade?', 'Need a place to stay in Kigali?', 'Hair loss is not the end of your story').
About half of the Rwandan ads running 60+ days are income-chain posts and 'earn 30K a day' recruiters: age is not a quality signal on its own.

tradeRoutes.when: The default in Rwanda: 22 of 51 Rwandan Facebook video ads use the 'Send WhatsApp message' button, and 35 of 51 put the number in the caption.
Kinyarwanda captions: the corpus's own call to action (Duhamagare 9, Twandikire 8), never a translation of 'click the link'.
13 of 51 Rwandan Facebook ads send people to the Instagram profile; still give the number.
Services, car hire, travel, restaurants taking orders by phone ('Call now' on 4 of 51).
Kigali restaurants that deliver through the VubaVuba app (only when the owner says so).
Walk-in shops, clinics, bars and restaurants: a landmark, not a street ('Next to DELIGHT HOTEL', 'opposite IPRC traffic lights', 'Makuza Peace Plaza, Room 35').
Cash-on-delivery sellers; the trust line. Only when the owner offers both.
Rare in Rwandan ads (the Sofar Kigali ticket ad is the exception): an opening. Only when the owner accepts MoMo.
YouTube Shorts have no ad button: end on a QR code, the number or the name to search.

firstComment.why: Under 20 Kigali Instagram reels, 72 of 177 comments (41%) ask the price, and the rest of the 86 questions ask where, about delivery and for the number, often the same question 6 to 10 times under one reel; sellers answered 46 of the 86, and 19 of 38 price replies only said 'DM'. One pinned answer covers them all.
